title: Seladelpar
overview: Seladelpar is used in combination with ursodiol to treat primary biliary cholangitis (PBC; a type of liver disease that destroys bile ducts, which allows bile to stay in the liver and cause damage) in people who cannot take ursodiol or in people who were not treated successfully with ursodiol alone. Seladelpar is in a class of medications called peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR)-delta agonists. It works by works by decreasing the production of bile in the liver.

sections.Before taking seladelpar,: tell your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to seladelpar, any other medications, or any of the ingredients in seladelpar capsules. Ask your pharmacist for a list of the ingredients.tell your doctor and pharmacist what other prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Your doctor may need to change the doses of your medications or monitor you carefully for side effects.if you are taking cholestyramine (Locolest, Prevalite), colestipol (Colestid), or colesevelam (Welchol), take them at least 4 hours before or 4 hours after seladelpar.tell your doctor if you have advanced liver disease, including liver cirrhosis (a disease which causes scarring of liver tissue). Your doctor may not want you not to take seladelpar.tell your doctor if you have or have ever had bile duct obstruction (blockage in the tubes that carry bile from the liver to the gallbladder and small intestine) or other liver problems or osteoporosis.tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breast-feeding. If you become pregnant while taking seladelpar, call your doctor.
sections.Some side effects can be serious. If you: broken bones or fracturesyellowing of the skin or eyespain or swelling in the upper right part of the stomachblack, tarry, or bloody stoolscoughing up or vomiting blood or something that looks like coffee groundsunusual tirednessmental changes such as confusion, slurred speech, or changes in mood or personalitySeladelpar may cause other side effects. Call your doctor if you have any unusual problems while taking this medication.If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may send a report to the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online (https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch) or by phone (1-800-332-1088).
